newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers close to Russian deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: De Beers close to Russian deal - paper.

text.p: De Beers Central Selling Organisation (CSO) could be close to a new deal to market Russia's diamonds, the Business Day newspaper said on Tuesday.
It reported Russian diamond officials as saying the text of the agreement was due to be completed this week.

The paper quoted a De Beers spokesman in London who said: "De Beers can confirm that constructive talks were held last week. The talks are continuing and both parties have agreed not to divulge details."
De Beers sells about 75 percent of the world's diamond production through its CSO, which posted record diamond sales of $2.748 billion in the first six months of 1996.
The diamond market was hit by uncertainty at the start of the year when Russian producers dallied in renewing a marketing deal with the CSO when it expired last December.
Large numbers of renegade gemstones found themselves directly on the open market, undermining the balance.

In February De Beers and Russia's Almazy Rossii Sakha signed a memorandum of understanding and Russia has indicated it was ready to sign the agreement now that the June/July presidential elections were over.
